openBlocker.summary: The Green Goods protocol recovery Safe live state does not match its frozen manifest configuration and violates the hard threshold floor.

failingConditions: sameOwnerSet against the frozen manifest owner set (assertExpectedRecoverySafe, garden-safe-owners.ts:489) — live has 4 of the 6 manifest owners
openBlocker.humanDecision2026_08_17: Afo accepted the live 1-of-4 configuration for this release and directed that it is not a blocker. The accepted configuration is recorded in code as GREEN_GOODS_ACCEPTED_RECOVERY_CONFIGURATION in script/deploy/garden-safe-owners.ts, alongside the existing DEV_GUILD_REVIEWED_OWNERS constant, and the final Garden Safe plan now returns zero blockers.
openBlocker.manifestLeftUnmodified: config/commitment-pooling-release.json still freezes this Safe as 2-of-6. Editing it was attempted and reverted: its hash is the release lock for commitment-pooling-settlement-credit-v1, and the Arbitrum pool-backfill lane has already broadcast all 19 of its boundaries bound to that hash. requireCompleteCheckpoint compares completed-lane checkpoints against the live manifest lock, so changing the manifest would retroactively invalidate mined work and stop the release operator from starting.
openBlocker.acceptedRisk: A single one of the four Green Goods signers reaches the Garden Safe threshold of two when combined with any other owner. Every other reviewed condition is still asserted.
openBlocker.note: Both resolutions require a live Safe transaction on 0x1B9A… that only its owners can execute. Because the Garden Safe initializer binds only the three owner addresses (garden-safe-owners.ts:300-319), changing this Safe's internal threshold or owner set does not move any of the 18 predicted Garden Safe addresses.
